# axiolid-mesh-compile

## Overview

The scalar reference compilers for an `axiolid-model` geometry graph.
`ReferenceMeshCompiler` walks the graph and produces one `TriMesh` per root:
it resolves instances and collections, composes transforms, tessellates
profiles, sweeps, B-reps and authored meshes, and hands booleans to whichever
`MeshBoolean` provider it is given. `ReferenceExactCompiler` compiles the
families it supports to exact B-reps, places instances under rigid
transforms, cuts placed openings from placed extrusions with the general
exact boolean, clips them by half-spaces through the same boolean, and
refuses the rest by name. `ReferenceMeshCompiler` also compiles curve
nodes (atomic 2D and 3D curves, open profiles, and their placements) to
polylines within a certified chord bound (`PolylineCompiler`). This crate
owns graph traversal and dispatch; the construction algorithms themselves
(profile flattening, extrusion, revolution, sweeps) belong to
`axiolid-construct`.

## Design notes

- The caller always supplies the tolerance through `ExecutionOptions`;
  there is no built-in default. Without an explicit chord budget, curves are
  flattened to the linear tolerance.
- Read volume through `CompileOutcome::solid_mesh`: a surface model can
  compile to a closed mesh without bounding a solid.
  A mesh is reported `MeshClosure::Solid` only when it is a closed,
  consistently wound two-manifold; a declared solid that tessellates open
  is `MeshClosure::OpenSolid`, and `solid_mesh` refuses it.
- Before a mesh boolean, operand coordinates a rounding residue from the
  other operand's axis-aligned faces (16 `f64::EPSILON` of the largest
  coordinate the operands reach, or their result reaches once an
  `Instance` places it, about `2e-8` at georeferenced coordinates) are set
  onto them exactly, so a tool a rounding error short of its host's face
  leaves no skin that thin, near the origin or placed far from it (#276,
  #312); a thicker skin is authored and kept whatever the tolerance
  (#291). The move is at most the tolerance, none
  at zero, and the deviation report names it
  (`deviation::SNAPPED_OPERANDS`). A boolean whose snapped operands are
  refused is cut as given, with no snap reported.

## Changes

Latest release, 0.3.25 (2026-10-14):

### Added

- A test of the deck of openbimrs/ifc#443 (#307): rectangles at stations
  0 and 5 along an offset by distances beside an ellipse, windowed by
  `1e-5`, compile to the window-free deck bitwise (about 10 by Pappus),
  and stations 30 along and within the window of the joint after the
  varying piece resolve, through `axiolid-evaluate`'s certified lengths
  of varying offsets.

### Fixed

- A boolean cut in its host's own frame and placed far from the origin
  no longer keeps a skin its placement folds (#312, ADR 0080 amendment).
  The snap closed residues only up to `16 f64::EPSILON` of the operands'
  own coordinates (about `1.3e-14` for a 3.67 m wall), so doors `2e-14` to
  `1e-10` short of a wall's face left a skin that thin, and once an
  `Instance` placed the wall 5600 km out its faces crossed and
  `enclosed_volume` refused the mesh as self-intersecting. The reach now
  covers the coordinates the result is placed at: `Instance` and
  `InstanceAtStation` carry the placed coordinate scale down to their
  source with the tolerance and the chord budget, and the snap reaches
  `16 f64::EPSILON` of it (about `2e-8` there), still capped at the
  tolerance and still landing only exactly; a micrometre skin stays. The
  compile cache keys on that scale, rounded up to three significant bits,
  so a source placed near and far compiles once per scale. The move is
  reported under `deviation::SNAPPED_OPERANDS` as before.
